title: Excellent blowup geometry and projective closed transforms
statement: Let $S$ be an excellent integral Noetherian scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subset\mathcal O_S$ be a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type which is the unit ideal on a nonempty open $U\subset S$. Set $T=\operatorname{Bl}_I S=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-relative-proj] and let $v:T\to S$ be its structure map. Then $T$ is excellent, integral and Noetherian, and $v$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and an isomorphism over $S\setminus V(I)$, hence birational. The degreewise multiplication surjection $\operatorname{Sym} I\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$ induces a closed immersion $T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(I)$, so $v$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. For any finite-projective-space projective morphism $X\to S$ [def-kun-projective] and any closed subscheme $Y\subset X\times_S T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product], $Y\to T$ is projective in the finite-projective-space sense. On every affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ with $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, the nonempty standard charts of $T$ have domain rings $A[I/a_j]\subset\operatorname{Frac}A$ for $a_j\ne0$; charts for $a_j=0$ are empty.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective (Sym-to-Rees closed immersion); More on Algebra Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent. Retained proof Steps 3--4 of the parent, including the two distinct projectivity conventions.

proof.text: The ideal sheaf $I$ is nonzero: at a point of the nonempty $U$ its stalk is the nonzero local ring of the integral $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-chart-density]. On each nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ and for generators $I|_V=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ it gives the indicated finite chart cover, with empty charts for zero generators and nonzero domain rings $B_j=A[I/a_j]\subset A_{a_j}$ otherwise. Since $A$ is a domain and $a_j\ne0$, the map $A_{a_j}\to\operatorname{Frac}A$, $x/a_j^n\mapsto x/a_j^n$, is injective: a zero fraction has numerator zero. Thus the displayed chart rings are subrings of $\operatorname{Frac}A$, as asserted. Put $W=S\setminus V(I)$; the same cited lemma gives that $W$ is a nonempty dense integral open of $S$ and $v^{-1}(W)$ meets every nonempty chart in a nonempty dense principal open.

By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $v^{-1}(W)\to W$ is an isomorphism. Step 1 makes this open dense in $T$: every nonempty open meets a chart and then its dense principal open. The domain chart cover makes $T$ reduced. Its dense open $v^{-1}(W)$ is nonempty irreducible, so $T$ is irreducible: any two nonempty opens meet this dense open and intersect there. Hence $T$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The isomorphism between the dense opens $v^{-1}(W)$ and $W$ proves birationality. Finite type of $I$ allows [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], giving properness of $v$. Proper includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; as $S$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $T$ is Noetherian.

proof.text: Choose an affine cover of $S$ by spectra of excellent rings, as in the definition of an excellent scheme (Morphisms, definition-excellent); [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] also ensures that every affine open of $S$ has an excellent ring. Above each member $\operatorname{Spec}A$ use Step 1. For $a_j\ne0$, $B_j=A[I/a_j]$ is generated over $A$ by the finite list $a_i/a_j$: if $x=\sum c_i a_i\in I$, then $x/a_j=\sum c_i(a_i/a_j)$, and by [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] these fractions generate the chart algebra. Thus $B_j$ is a finite type $A$-algebra. Apply [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with multiplicative set $\{1\}$ to conclude that $B_j$ is excellent. These charts cover $T$, so $T$ is excellent by the same affine-cover definition; [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] gives the assertion for every affine open of $T$ as well.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent; morphisms.tex definition-excellent and Tag 0HAB, lemma-locally-excellent

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-rees-symmetric-presentation] with $X=S$ and $\mathcal I=I$. It supplies the quasi-coherent sheaf Rees algebra $\mathcal R=\bigoplus I^n$, its canonical affine graded identifications (identity in degree zero, compatible with affine restriction), and the degreewise-surjective multiplication morphism $\varphi:\operatorname{Sym}I\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal R$. These are precisely the inputs of [lem-sfb-rees-presentation-blowup-immersion] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal R$: it identifies the ordinary blowup with $\operatorname{Proj}_S\mathcal R$ and gives the closed immersion induced by $\varphi$, $T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(I)$, whose structural composite is $v$. The sheaf $I$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type, so taking $\mathcal E=I$ in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] proves projectivity in the projective-bundle sense.

Choose the closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$ given by [def-kun-projective]. Its base change along $T\to S$ is a closed immersion $X\times_S T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S\times_S T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The cartesian projective-space square of [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] identifies its target over $T$ with $\mathbf P^N_T$. Compose this immersion with the given $Y\hookrightarrow X\times_S T$; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] makes the resulting $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_T$ a closed immersion. Both arrows are over $T$, so its structural composite is the given $Y\to T$. This is the finite-projective-space condition of [def-kun-projective], with the same $N$. No flatness of $v$ or nonemptiness of $Y$ is needed.
